# Overview

This R Markdown file describes the NPS prior approach to logistic regression specified in Salvatore et al. (2024), 
including the four priors

1. Mixed-Distance  
2. Mixed-Distance-log  
3. Mixed-Distance-log10  
4. Power Prior

We present the model setup, prior definitions, and the MCMC algorithms implementing these methods.

# Model Specification

We observe a probability sample (PS) \((y_i, \mathbf{x}_i)\) for \(i = 1,\ldots,n\) and a nonprobability sample (NPS) \((\tilde{y}_\ell, \tilde{\mathbf{x}}_\ell)\) for \(\ell = 1,\ldots,\tilde{n}\). The logistic model is

\[
y_i \mid \boldsymbol{\beta} \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\theta_i), \qquad 
\theta_i = \frac{\exp(\mathbf{x}_i'\boldsymbol{\beta})}{1 + \exp(\mathbf{x}_i'\boldsymbol{\beta})}.
\]

so each likelihood contribution is 

\[
p(y_i \mid {\beta}) = \frac{\exp({x}_i'{\beta})^{y_i}}{[1 + \exp({x}_i'{\beta})]}
\]

# Pseudolikelihood

Given weights $w_1, \ldots, w_n$ equal to the inverse probabilities of selection in the PS after rescaling to sum to the sample 
size $n$, we exponentiate the likelihood contributions as 

\[
\tilde{p}(y_i \mid {\beta}) = \frac{\exp({x}_i'{\beta})^{w_i y_i}}{[1 + \exp({x}_i'{\beta})]^{w_i}}
\]

A likelihood-based model is recovered by setting each weight to 1.

# Prior Specification

## Mixed-Distance Priors: General Form

The general form is

\[
\boldsymbol{\beta} \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{NPS}, \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\ldots,\sigma_p^2)).
\]

### HMC Implementation

We target the log posterior

\[
\log p(\beta \mid \cdot) =
\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i \log \text{Bernoulli}\left(y_i \mid \text{logit}^{-1}(x_i'\beta)\right)
\, + \,
\log \mathcal{N}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{NPS}, \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\ldots,\sigma_p^2)).
\]

Equivalently, using the logit link, the log-likelihood terms are

\[
\log p(y_i \mid \beta) = y_i (x_i'\beta) - \log\{1 + \exp(x_i'\beta)\}
\]

```{stanmodel}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;                    // PS sample size
  int<lower=1> p;                    // number of predictors

  matrix[n, p] X;                    // PS design matrix

  array[n] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;  // PS outcomes

  vector<lower=0>[n] w;              // PS weights (rescaled to sum to n)

  vector[p] beta_prior_mean;         // beta hat NPS (will calculate in R)
  vector<lower=0>[p] beta_prior_sd;  // sigma_j
}

parameters {
  vector[p] beta;
}

model {
  // Prior
  beta ~ normal(beta_prior_mean, beta_prior_sd);

  // Pseudolikelihood (only PS)
  for (i in 1:n) {
    target += w[i] * bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y[i] | X[i] * beta);
  }
}
```

We fit this model for each of the three following variations on the mixed-distance prior.

### Mixed-Distance

\[
\sigma_j = |\hat{\beta}_{PS,j} - \hat{\beta}_{NPS,j}|.
\]

### Mixed-Distance-log

\[
\sigma_j = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\log \tilde{n}} \max\{(\hat{\beta}_{PS,j}-\hat{\beta}_{NPS,j})^2,\, \hat{\sigma}^2_{NPS,j}\}}.
\]

### Mixed-Distance-log10

\[
\sigma_j = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\log_{10} \tilde{n}} \max\{(\hat{\beta}_{PS,j}-\hat{\beta}_{NPS,j})^2,\, \hat{\sigma}^2_{NPS,j}\}}.
\]


## Power Prior

A power prior on $\beta$ is

\[
p(\beta \mid \tilde{y}, \tilde{X}) \propto L(\beta \mid \tilde{y},\tilde{X})^a \, p(\beta),
\]

with a fixed exponent \(a\). The authors set \(a\) equal to the \(p\)-value resulting from a 
Hotelling \(T^2\) test of equality between \(\hat{\beta}_{PS}\) and \(\hat{\beta}_{NPS}\). They also 
place a \(t_3(0, 2.5)\) prior on each coefficient, resulting in the 
posterior distribution
\[
p(\beta \mid \text{data}) \propto 
\left\{ \prod_{i = 1}^n \frac{\exp({x}_i'{\beta})^{w_i y_i}}{[1 + \exp({x}_i'{\beta})]^{w_i}}  \right\}
\left\{ \prod_{\ell = 1}^{\tilde{n}} \frac{\exp(\tilde{x}_\ell'{\beta})^{a \tilde{y}_\ell}}{[1 + \exp(\tilde{x}_\ell'{\beta})]^{a}} \right\} 
\left\{\prod_{j=1}^p t_3(\beta_j \mid 0, 2.5)\right\}
\]

### HMC Implementation 

In the Stan implementation, we target the following log posterior:

\[
\log p(\beta \mid \cdot) =
\sum_{i=1}^{n} w_i \log \text{Bernoulli}\left(y_i \mid \text{logit}^{-1}(x_i'\beta)\right)
\, + \,
a \sum_{\ell=1}^{\tilde{n}} \log \text{Bernoulli}\left(\tilde{y}_\ell \mid \text{logit}^{-1}(\tilde{x}_\ell'\beta)\right)
\, + \,
\sum_{j=1}^{p} \log t_3(\beta_j \mid 0, 2.5).
\]

Equivalently, using the logit link, the log-likelihood terms are

\[
\log p(y_i \mid \beta) = y_i (x_i'\beta) - \log\{1 + \exp(x_i'\beta)\},
\qquad
\log p(\tilde{y}_\ell \mid \beta) = \tilde{y}_\ell (\tilde{x}_\ell'\beta) - \log\{1 + \exp(\tilde{x}_\ell'\beta)\}.
\]

```{stanmodel}
data {
  int<lower=1> n;                 // PS sample size
  int<lower=1> n_np;              // NPS sample size
  int<lower=1> p;                 // number of coefficients

  matrix[n, p] X;                 // PS design matrix
  matrix[n_np, p] X_np;           // NPS design matrix

  array[n] int<lower=0, upper=1> y;        // PS outcomes
  array[n_np] int<lower=0, upper=1> y_np;  // NPS outcomes

  vector<lower=0>[n] w;           // PS weights (rescaled to sum to n)
  real<lower=0, upper=1> a;       // power prior exponent
}

parameters {
  vector[p] beta;
}

model {
  // Prior: t_3(0, 2.5)
  beta ~ student_t(3, 0, 2.5);

  // PS pseudolikelihood
  for (i in 1:n) {
    target += w[i] * bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y[i] | X[i] * beta);
  }

  // NPS likelihood (power prior)
  for (l in 1:n_np) {
    target += a * bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y_np[l] | X_np[l] * beta);
  }
}
```

# References

Salvatore, C., Biffignandi, S., Sakshaug, J., Wiśniowski, A., Struminskaya, B., 
"Bayesian Integration of Probability and Nonprobability Samples for Logistic Regression," 
Journal of Survey Statistics and Methodology, Volume 12, Issue 2, April 2024, Pages 458–492, 
https://doi.org/10.1093/jssam/smad041.
